draft.title: Changing biomes to grow more food
card: A biome is a large area with a similar climate, soil, plants and animals. People change biomes so that more food can be grown on the land.
Clearing and draining
Clearing vegetation removes trees and shrubs to make room for crops or grazing. Draining wetlands removes standing water so the wet ground can be farmed.
Irrigating and terracing
Irrigating brings water to dry land through channels, pipes or sprinklers. Terracing cuts flat steps into a steep slope so crops can be planted on it.
Fertilisers
Adding fertilisers puts extra nutrients into the soil. This helps crops grow better on soil that is poor in nutrients.
draft.remember: People change biomes to grow more food by changing the plants, water, slope or soil.

a.q: Which change to a biome is terracing?
opts: Cutting flat steps into a steep hillside to plant crops
Bringing water to dry land through channels and pipes
Removing trees and shrubs to make room for grazing
Adding extra nutrients to soil that is poor in them
a.why: Terracing cuts flat steps into a slope so crops can be planted on it. Irrigating is the tempting wrong option, because it also helps crops grow, but it changes the water supply, not the shape of the slope.
a.clue: Think about what is done to the shape of the land.

b.q: Dev farms on a dry plain. He builds channels to carry water from a nearby river to his paddocks. Which change is he making to the biome?
opts: Irrigating the land
Terracing the land
Draining a wetland
Clearing vegetation
b.why: Dev is bringing water to dry land, which is irrigating. Draining a wetland is the opposite, because it removes water from wet ground.
b.clue: Is water being added to the land or taken away?

a.best: Cutting flat steps into a steep hillside to plant crops
